newsitem.title: USA: Family Bargain hurt by costs, write-offs.
newsitem.headline: Family Bargain hurt by costs, write-offs.

text.p: Family Bargain Corp said on Friday that its 1997 full-year financial results were hurt by lower gross profit margins, higher costs and some unusual, non-recurring charges, but the company now has the financing it needs to expand in the coming year.
Family Bargain reported a net loss of $9.07 per share for the year ending February 1, compared with a loss of $0.51 for the year before.
The company attributed the wider loss in part to lower gross profit margins due to liquidity constraints and higher inventory shrinkage.

Family Bargain also cited higher operating expenses as a percentage of sales due to increased labor costs, an increased store-closing allowance and $19.5 million in charges from shutting down the New York office and from various writeoffs, including impairment of goodwill from the Factory 2-U acquisition.
But Family Bargain said a recent equity investment has given it the financing necessary to expand, and it plans to open 20 new stores in the current year.
Family Bargain operates 157 off-price retail stores selling clothing and household goods.
